paragraphs: This page covers services that foster across Scotland. In Scotland you can foster with your local council, an independent agency or a charity; mygov.scot lists a fostering contact for each of the 32 councils, and the Care Inspectorate registers the other services. Many council areas have their own page on this site, including Glasgow, Edinburgh, Fife, Aberdeen, Renfrewshire, Inverclyde, Argyll and Bute, North Lanarkshire and South Lanarkshire.

To foster in Scotland you need to live in the UK full time, be 18 or over and have a spare bedroom, although some services set a minimum age of 21 and some councils make exceptions on the bedroom depending on the child's age. There is no upper age limit, and you can foster whether you rent or own, work full time or already have children.

The Scottish Recommended Allowance is the national minimum level of support for foster and kinship carers. For 2026-27 it rose by 3.8 per cent to £177.68 a week for a child aged 0 to 4, £206.71 for ages 5 to 15 and £283.35 for young people of 16 and over. It covers the allowance only; any fee for the carer comes on top and is set by each fostering service. Councils pay it for their own carers, and independent agencies pay it for theirs.

Becoming a carer starts with home visits and preparation groups, followed by an assessment that mygov.scot says can take 6 to 12 months, with checks on health, finances, references and your home. A fostering panel then makes a recommendation, and approved carers are reviewed after the first year and then every two years.
Talk to two or three of the services above, including your local council, and ask what fee they pay on top of the allowance.
